reason: The cited evidence (E2) shows that vacuum heat treatment at 500°C improves wear resistance in a different HEA coating system, but it does not address FeNiCrCoCu, thin films, selective Cr/Cu oxidation, or oxidizing environments. E1 is entirely about a different alloy and property (corrosion), providing no support. Thus, none of the specific key premises are supported by the cited passages.
premises: Pre-oxidation at 500°C forms a continuous, self-healing Cr- and Cu-enriched oxide layer on FeNiCrCoCu
This oxide layer reduces metal-to-metal contact and friction, enhancing wear resistance
Heat treatment at 500°C refines the microstructure to a nanocrystalline state, increasing hardness
Increased hardness from microstructural refinement reduces wear rates
The combined oxide layer and refined microstructure provide superior high-temperature wear resistance over as-deposited coatings
